questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Row Operation That's Equivalent To Left Multiplication by an Elementary Matrix
questions.problem: Let $E=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the row operation that, when applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ gives the result of the product $EA.$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $E$ is obtained by multiplying the first row of the identity matrix  by $-4$:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the row operation ${R}_{1}:=-4{R}_{1}$ to $A.$

We need to find an elementary matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:=18{R}_{1}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$

$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}18 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix Product That's Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations
questions.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations, in the given order, are to be applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A:$

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}
$$

Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the two given elementary row operations.

- The first elementary row operation is ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second elementary row operation is ${R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$ 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix Product That's Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations
questions.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations, in the given order, are to be applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A:$

$$
{R}_{2}:=-2{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}
$$

Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the two given elementary row operations.

- The first elementary row operation is ${R}_{2}:=-2{R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:=-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second elementary row operation is ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- The third elementary row operation is ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{3}$ on the left and get ${E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$
